newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM backs cutting government to save money.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM backs cutting government to save money.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Tuesday said he was happy that the largest party in the government was recalling several of its ministers to save money and streamline the government.
Shkele is pushing through a budget for 1997 that calls for balanced books and spending cuts. The deficit in 1996 is planned at 40 million lats after 90 million lats in 1995.

The Democratic Party Saimnieks, one of the most influential parties in the six-party coalition, said late Monday it was recalling three state ministers and wanted to further cut the number of state officials by 10 to 30 percent.
"I am glad that politicians have understood that so big and so expensive a government is not right for a country facing such difficulties," Prime Minister Andris Skele told Latvian Radio.
The Democratic Party said the move would save millions of lats that could be spent elsewhere.
The deficit-free budget has caused controversy, particularly among state employees and teachers, who say they are being asked to make too large sacrifices.
Shkele has repeatedly said he wants to improve the work of the government and make it more efficient.
"The government is too big, too heavy, too inefficient. My plan has been accepted and I am glad," Shkele added.
